source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Elevated blood pressure, because either the systolic value is at least 120 mm Hg or the diastolic value is at least 80 mm Hg.","B":"Stage 1 hypertension, because a systolic value above 110 mm Hg is enough to meet the current blood-pressure category for hypertension.","C":"Normal blood pressure, because 118/76 mm Hg is below the AHA cutoffs of 120 systolic and 80 diastolic for the normal category.","D":"Stage 2 hypertension, because a diastolic value above 70 mm Hg is sufficient to meet the current threshold for stage 2 hypertension."}}
source_row.rationale: Current AHA categories define normal blood pressure as systolic below 120 mm Hg and diastolic below 80 mm Hg. Option C is correct because 118/76 mm Hg meets both criteria. Option A incorrectly calls the reading elevated even though systolic is below 120 and diastolic is below 80. Option B uses a nonstandard systolic threshold to diagnose stage 1 hypertension. Option D uses a nonstandard diastolic threshold to diagnose stage 2 hypertension.
